title: Enough for now
hook: a present judgment, a present act, a present acceptance: that's enough (Meditations 9.6)

segments.voice: Yesterday's word was George Long, whose translation says the wrongdoer wrongs himself. Your line was he's hurt himself.

Your phone shows you a hundred things you could want. A better kitchen, a different job, a calmer family, the trip, the body, the version of you that's on top of everything. The list never ends because it isn't built to end. Then, in book nine, Marcus writes an entry only one sentence long, and in George Long's English it finishes on a word that list never says. Enough.
screen: `A HUNDRED THINGS TO WANT.` → `A LIST BUILT NOT TO END.` → `ENOUGH FOR NOW.`

segments.voice: Marcus writes, roughly: your present judgment, grasping things as they are; your present action, done for the common good; your present acceptance of whatever comes from outside you. These are enough. Look at the parts. A judgment: seeing this moment truly. An action: doing this moment's work for others. An acceptance: being at peace with what this moment brought. Each one happens now. None of them needs a future that hasn't arrived. That's why enough is radical. So much of what drives us says not yet: not until the promotion, the cure, the apology. Marcus says the three things a good life needs are all available in the present, and that's sufficient. Not perfect. Sufficient. The Greek verb behind that word means it suffices. And the week, looking back: the spring runs clear, poured out, teach or bear, we're one fabric, nature's work, he's hurt himself, and now, it suffices. Seven entries, and every one pulls the same way: away from what other people do and what tomorrow might bring, toward what you can see, do and accept right here. Across books eight and nine, the lesson keeps coming back to the same small size: this moment, and three things you can do in it.
screen: `JUDGMENT, ACTION, ACCEPTANCE.` · `ALL THREE HAPPEN NOW.` · `NOT PERFECT. SUFFICIENT.` · `A WEEK OF WHAT'S HERE.` · then, large: `IT SUFFICES.`

segments.voice: Name one thing about this exact moment you've been fighting, the noise, the tiredness, the weather, and without pretending to like it, say inside: this is what's here. Then check the three: am I seeing this moment truly, is there something good I can do in it, can I accept what it brought? If you can answer, that's enough.
Three presents. Marcus's list: a true judgment, an action for the common good, an acceptance of what comes. They suffice. Today's word.
Your line: it suffices. Judgment, action, acceptance: not perfect, just sufficient. That's the week, done.

howItsDone: Some readers of the Meditations use this entry as a short evening check: did I see truly, act for others, and accept what came today? If so, the day was enough.

what it means: the three things a good life needs, seeing truly, acting well, accepting what comes, are all available now, and they suffice.
what a scholar hears: the three match a pattern the scholar Pierre Hadot traced through the Meditations: disciplines of judgment, of action, and of desire or acceptance.
